title: Facebook Ads Coach or Agency: Which Should You Hire in 2026?
summary: Hire a Facebook ads coach to sharpen a team that already runs the account, or an agency to produce ads and run campaigns. Compare the work each option covers.
body_markdown:
## Which one fits your situation?


Match the option to the gap you actually have.


Your situation Better fit Why


Nobody can produce or launch ads every week Agency, such as Knowlify with Meta management The gap is output


You have a media buyer but no new creative Creative-only agency Your buyer launches; the agency supplies ads


You have a buyer and creative, but results are flat Coach The gap is judgment and test design


You plan to bring the account in-house within a year Coach, with an agency in the meantime The gap is knowledge your team will need to keep


If you hire only a creative agency, make sure your buyer can act on the test results. Finished ads without a person who launches and reads them rarely improve the account. Many teams use both: a coach diagnoses the account and sets the test plan, while an agency produces the concepts and runs the campaigns, both working from the same customer problem.


## Who should own the ad account?


Whichever route you choose, the ad account, pixel and Pages should sit in your own business. Meta's[business asset management documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management) describes an agency as a business that can manage or access assets owned by another business and perform specific tasks on the client's behalf.


Meta's[business-to-business guide](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management/guides/business-to-business) describes the business that owns an ad account adding an agency with specific permitted tasks, such as advertise and analyze. By our reading, that means switching agencies is a matter of removing one partner's access and adding another's, not rebuilding campaigns. Ask every provider to work inside an account you own.


## How do you check an agency's credentials?


A Meta Business Partner badge is one signal. Meta's[Business Partners program](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing-partners) says eligibility varies by solution type and is typically based on the quantity and quality of a company's work across Meta technologies. A badge is not a promise of results, so ask for scope in writing: which campaigns, how many new concepts each month, and which metrics the agency reports. Our[how to choose a Facebook ads agency guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) lists the questions to ask.


Also ask who owns tracking. Meta's[Conversions API documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api) describes it as a connection between an advertiser's marketing data, from a server, website platform, app or CRM, and Meta systems, meant to optimize ad targeting, decrease cost per result and measure outcomes. Ask each finalist who sets up these events and who fixes them when they stop arriving.


## What do agency fees look like next to a coach?


Coach fees are not in our sources, so we cannot compare them with agency fees directly. Agency fees do have published reference points.[Top Growth Marketing](https://topgrowthmarketing.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) says its fees range from $2,000 to $10,000 per month depending on ad spend volume and scope, with $3,000 as the low end in its comparison table, and its engagements are month-to-month. It describes its clients as DTC ecommerce brands spending $5,000 to $500,000 a month on ads.


[Adside AI](https://www.adside.ai/pricing) lists 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum, covering strategy, creative production, launch, optimization and reporting. Knowlify quotes privately by scope.


Those fees buy a different responsibility than a coaching session. A coach's hours are advice your team must carry out, while an agency fee pays for finished ads and campaign work. Compare them by the work each covers, not by the monthly number alone.


## Key takeaways


- Hire a coach when the gap is knowledge and your team can carry out the advice. Hire an agency when the gap is production and campaign ownership.
- Knowlify is our top pick for finished AI video ads with optional Meta campaign management, and it is an agency rather than a coaching program.
- Keep the ad account in your own business, whichever route you choose.
- Ask for scope in writing, including who sets up and fixes the Conversions API events.
- Compare fees by the work each covers, because the coach fees we looked for were not published.


## FAQ


### Is a Facebook ads coach cheaper than an agency?


We could not verify coach fees from published sources, so we cannot say. The cheaper option is the one whose output your team can use. A coach costs your team hours to carry out the advice, while an agency costs a fee for finished work and campaign responsibility. Compare both at your real staffing level.


### What does a Facebook ads agency charge?


Published examples vary. Top Growth Marketing says $2,000 to $10,000 per month depending on ad spend volume and scope, Adside AI lists 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum, and Knowlify prices private quotes by scope. Ask for the monthly fee, any setup fee and charges for extra creative, then add media spend as a separate line.


### Can I hire a coach and an agency together?


Yes. A coach can diagnose the account and review results, while an agency produces ads and runs campaigns. Make sure both work from the same customer problem and the same test plan.


### Who should own the ad account?


You should. Keep the ad account, pixel and Pages in your own business and give the provider access. That lets you change providers without rebuilding your campaigns.


### Does a Meta Business Partner badge guarantee results?


No. Meta says eligibility varies by solution type and is typically based on the quantity and quality of a company's work across Meta technologies. Treat the badge as one signal, and verify the scope, the reporting and the people who will work on your account.


### What should I check before signing an agency contract?


Check the monthly fee, the setup charge, the number of finished ads, revision rounds, the minimum term and the cancellation terms. Confirm who owns the ad account, the pixel and the creative files, and get the test plan and reporting cadence in writing.
